summary: Queued metadata update flood causes GPU attach throttling and batched-route throughput degradation for dedicated tenant
description: Issue summary: Since ~2026-03-13T14:05 UTC we observed a sustained drop in batched-route throughput for Quantux Financial's dedicated pool. Impact: p50->p99 latency increase and effective throughput decline for their critical batched prediction routes, causing request backlogs and request timeouts. Observed behavior: Autoscaler showed normal target capacity but allocator attach times spiked and GPU attach failures / backoff increased, leading to slot starvation. We observed a high rate of small metadata update operations queued on the control plane (~40K/min) coincident with the event window. Time window: 2026-03-13T14:05 to ongoing. Initial hypothesis: A metadata-update flood (operator-side background job within customer's workloads) caused control plane/allocator RPC queueing that slowed attach handshakes and amplified small-stream fanout, which in turn caused noisy-tenant-like GPU attach throttles and autoscaler mis-predictions.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Route a high-rate series of tiny metadata update calls (simulated from a dedicated tenant) that trigger control plane reconciliation (10-50K ops/min)
2) Simultaneously drive a steady stream of short batched inference requests to the tenant's reserved pool (many small streams)
3) Observe allocator attach latency, failed attach retries, and autoscaler not increasing capacity proportionally
4) Verify GPU slot utilization and per-GPU attach failure rates via allocator and runtime dashboards

metrics_snapshot: baseline p50 latency (batch route): 95ms -> degraded to 220ms
control-plane metadata op rate: 1.2K/min -> 40K/min during incident
gpu slot utilization for pool: 72% steady but effective available slots reported as 10% due to attach backlog
investigation_notes: Support triage: Verified customer impact and elevated to SRE due to pod/allocator attach signals
Telemetry shows a correlation between metadata op rate spikes and attach latency increases (strong temporal overlap)
Autoscaler logic used recent attach success rate and CPU signals; with attach retries the autoscaler suppressed scale-up to avoid flapping
Allocator backlog queues contain many short-lived attach requests interleaved with metadata reconciliation RPCs — observed a control-plane thread pool exhaustion window
No kernel-level GPU errors found on hosts; NVLink and driver logs normal
Customer confirmed a recent deploy of a background metadata sync (internal service) that increased update frequency to config store
We reproduced attach latency in staging by replaying metadata update traffic and short batched streams, matching degraded tail latencies
workaround: 1) Applied temporary rate-limiting on customer's metadata-update path at the API gateway for tenant quantux-prod (throttle to 2K/min). 2) Increased allocator attach thread pool from 32->64 in the region to reduce control-plane queueing (hotfix). 3) Enabled a short-term autoscaler override to permit emergency scale-up for the customer's pool.
resolution_notes: Mitigation steps reduced attach latency and restored batched-route throughput to near baseline. Throttle on metadata updates kept control-plane queueing within acceptable bounds while customer rolled back their high-frequency metadata job. Allocator thread pool increase will be evaluated for global rollout. Autoscaler override reverted after steady state observed.
follow_up_items: Engineering: implement more granular backpressure between control-plane metadata ops and allocator RPCs (tech debt ticket OPEN)
Product: add tenant-specific metadata-rate quotas for dedicated pools and surface proactive alerts
SRE: add a synthetic canary that exercises attach handshake under metadata load to detect regressions
Support: notify Quantux Financial CSM and schedule joint post-incident call (within 48 hours)
